extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents/attorneys, and patent examiners handling PCT international-phase filings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing supplementary international search, international publication, omission and withdrawal of PCT applications, international preliminary examination (Chapter II), Demands, and permitted amendments during the international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the supplementary international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplementary international search report need not contain the citation of any document cited in the international search report, except where the document needs to be cited in conjunction with other documents that were not cited in the international search report. The supplementary international search report may contain explanations with regard to the citations of the documents considered to be relevant and with regard to the scope of the supplementary international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIS reports focus on additional citations not redundant with the main ISR unless a prior-cited document must be cited together with other documents; the SISA may add explanatory text about relevance and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review outcomes for challenged ISA opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on review, the reviewer finds that the opinion was partially unjustified but still considers the application does not comply with unity requirement, it shall notify the applicant and proceed as provided. If it finds the opinion was entirely unjustified, it shall notify the applicant, establish the supplementary international search report on all parts of the international application and refund the review fee to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions after review must be communicated to the applicant; a full reversal triggers establishment of SIS on all parts and refund of the review fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and effect of the supplementary international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search shall, on the same day, transmit one copy of the supplementary international search report (or declaration that none will be established) to the International Bureau and one copy to the applicant. Subject to exceptions, Article 20(1) and certain Rules shall apply as if the supplementary international search report were part of the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIS is sent promptly to both IB and applicant; however, IPEA need not take SIS into account if received after it has begun drawing up its written opinion or report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence and limitations of International Searching Authorities for SIS
rubrics_metrics.description: An International Searching Authority shall be competent to carry out supplementary international searches if its preparedness to do so is stated in the applicable agreement under Article 16(3)(b), subject to any limitations and conditions set out in that agreement. The ISA that carried out the main international search shall not be competent to carry out a supplementary international search for that same application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations may include subject-matter restrictions (beyond Article 17(2)), limits on the total number of SIS in a period, and limits that SIS will not extend beyond a certain number of claims. Check the SISA agreements (Annex SISA) for specified limitations and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose, scope and procedural requirements for requesting SIS
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplementary international search (SIS) is an optional service to allow additional searches by a SISA during the international phase, expanding linguistic and technical scope and reducing risk of new prior art in national phases. SIS will be carried out on the application as filed and will only cover one invention or group of inventions having unity of invention; there is no option for paying additional fees to search multiple inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for SIS must be filed prior to the expiration of 22 months from the priority date, submitted directly to the IB (not to individual SISAs), accompanied by a supplementary search handling fee (IB) and a supplementary search fee set by each SISA, payable in Swiss francs within one month. Applicants from certain States may be eligible for a 90% reduction in the handling fee. If the main ISA identified lack of unity before SIS is requested, SIS can be requested to concentrate on a non-first claimed invention (PCT Rule 45 bis.1(d)). SIS results not in English will be translated into English by the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for international publication (PCT Article 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall publish international applications promptly after the expiration of 18 months from the priority date. The applicant may ask the IB to publish any time before that 18-month time limit. The international search report or the declaration referred to in Article 17(2)(a) shall be published as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No international publication occurs if the application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn before technical preparations for publication are completed. Language and form are governed by the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effects of international publication (PCT Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as protection in a designated State is concerned, the effects of international publication shall be the same as those which the national law provides for compulsory national publication of unexamined national applications, subject to paragraphs (2)–(4) which allow national law to condition effects on translations or other acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated States may require publication/availability of a translation (published translation, made available for public inspection, transmission to an unauthorized user, or combinations thereof) before the effects arise. National law may also make effects applicable only from receipt of a copy of the published international application in the national Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication numbering standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB shall assign to each published international application an international publication number different from the international application number consisting of 'WO' + four‑digit year + '/' + six‑digit serial number (e.g., 'WO 2004/123456').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This number is used on the published international application and in the Gazette entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for omission of information from publication (PCT Rule 48.2(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB shall, upon a reasoned request by the applicant received prior to completion of technical preparations for publication, omit from publication any information if it finds that: (i) the information does not obviously serve the purpose of informing the public about the application; (ii) publication would clearly prejudice the personal or economic interests of any person; and (iii) there is no prevailing public interest to have access to that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices/ISAs/IPEA/IB may suggest to the applicant to request omission. Where the IB omits information that also appears in files held by other Offices/Authorities, the IB shall promptly notify them; those Offices/Authorities must not provide access to the omitted information. The IB will not provide access to documents relating to the omission request either.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of international application, designations or priority claims (time limits and basics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the international application, the designation of any designated State, or a priority claim at any time prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Withdrawal shall be effective on receipt of a notice addressed by the applicant to the IB, the receiving Office or, where Article 39(1) applies, to the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of withdrawal received by the IB before technical preparations for publication are completed will prevent international publication. A withdrawal may be conditional (effective only if publication can still be prevented); if the condition cannot be met the withdrawal is not effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and representative rules for withdrawals (Rule 90 bis.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any notice of withdrawal referred to in Rules 90 bis.1 to 90 bis.4 shall be signed by the applicant or, if there are two or more applicants, by all of them. An appointed agent or appointed common representative may sign on behalf of those who appointed him, but an applicant considered the common representative may not sign on behalf of the other applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature formalities are strict; waivers of power of attorney provisions do not apply to withdrawals under PCT Rule 90 bis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal where processing/examination already started
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal under Rule 90 bis of the international application, any designation, any priority claim, the demand or any election shall have no effect in any designated or elected Office where the processing or examination has already started under Article 23(2) or Article 40(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal cannot undo processing/examination already underway in national or regional Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the international preliminary examination (IPEA examiner duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the demand is checked for compliance, the examiner shall study the description, drawings, claims, documents describing prior art cited in the international search report, and the written opinion established by the ISA. Furthermore, the examiner shall search at least to the point of bringing the previous search up to date and any new prior art discovered and applied must be made of record (see Rule 66.1ter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA's task includes evaluating prior art and updating searches; new art must be entered into the record so it will be available to applicant and Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ISA written opinion as first written opinion of IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: A further written opinion is usually not mandatory where the written opinion of the ISA is treated as the first written opinion of the IPEA. The U.S. IPEA will treat any written opinion of the ISA established by USPTO, EPO, KIPO, IP Australia, ILPO, JPO, or IPOS as the first written opinion of the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the ISA's written opinion is adopted as the IPEA's first opinion, no further written opinion need be issued before the international preliminary examination report even if objections remain outstanding; the examiner will consider applicant comments/amendments when establishing the IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for issuing a further written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: A further written opinion should be prepared by the examiner if applicant files a response that includes a persuasive argument that the written opinion issued by the ISA was improper because of a negative opinion with respect to lack of novelty, inventive step (non‑obviousness) or industrial applicability as described in PCT Article 33(2)–(4), and which results in the examiner considering any claims to lack novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability based on new art not necessitated by any amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A further written opinion is driven by persuasive applicant submissions that identify improper negative findings based on newly applied art (not caused by applicant amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of the further written opinion (PCT Rule 66.2 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any further written opinion should set forth, as applicable: (A) defects concerning subject matter not required to be examined or unclear/inadequately supported (Article 34(4)); (B) negative findings on claims for lack of novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability; (C) defects in form or contents; (D) findings that an amendment goes beyond the original disclosure; (E) observations on clarity of claims/description/drawings or support of claims (Rule 66.2); (F) decisions not to carry out IPE on a claim for which no ISR was issued; (G) if no acceptable sequence listing is available to allow meaningful IPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The further written opinion must fully state reasons for the opinion and identify defects so applicant can reply and amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for further written opinion and applicant reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The further written opinion is prepared on Form PCT/IPEA/408 to notify applicant of defects. The examiner is required to fully state reasons for the opinion (Rule 66.2(b)) and invite a written reply, normally setting a 2‑month time limit for the reply (Rule 66.2(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may reply with amendments and/or arguments. The U.S. rules permit a second written opinion in some situations if time allows. Replies received after the time limit are not normally considered, but amendments requested by the examiner or later amendments that put the application in better condition may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand filing requirements and effects (Chapter II Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing a proper Demand in an application for which the US IPEA is competent and for which fees have been paid, the international application shall be the subject of an international preliminary examination. The Demand shall be made on a standardized form (PCT Rule 53). The preliminary examination fee and handling fee shall be due within the applicable time limit set in Rule 57.3. Withdrawal of a proper Demand prior to the start of IPE entitles applicant to a refund of the preliminary examination fee minus the transmittal fee. Any Demand filed after the applicable time limit shall be considered as not submitted (Rule 54 bis.1(b)). The filing of a Demand constitutes the election of all Contracting States designated and bound by Chapter II (PCT Rule 53.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PCT/IPEA/401 and the fee calculation sheet; ensure timeliness and fee payment to create a valid Demand. Filing a Demand enables Chapter II examination and amendments under Article 34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right and formalities for amendments during international preliminary examination (PCT Article 34, Rule 66.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall have a right to amend the claims, description, and drawings in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed time limit before the international preliminary examination report is established. The amendment shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. Rule 66.8 requires, subject to paragraph (b), a replacement sheet for every sheet that differs, accompanied by a letter drawing attention to differences, indicating the basis for the amendment in the application as filed and preferably explaining the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where amendment is deletion or minor alteration, a copy of the relevant sheet containing alterations may be used if clarity is maintained. Cancellation of an entire sheet should be communicated in a letter explaining reasons. When amending claims, Rule 46.5 applies mutatis mutandis and the set of claims submitted replaces all previously filed claims. Under 37 CFR 1.485, amendments may be made at the time of filing the Demand or within the time limit set by the IPEA, but must comply with Rule 66.8.
